propositions: nested pytest child process in tests/_store_isolation.py omits --basetemp, causing it to join the user-global pytest numbered temp root instead of using caller-owned private directory

pytest session shutdown performs synchronous recursive deletion of stale numbered temp trees at cleanup_numbered_dir, which can consume the entire 90-second child timeout even after the selected test reports 100%

controlled A/B filesystem test with 400,000 stale temp entries showed shared-root cleanup took 10.8s versus private-basetemp cleanup took 0.882s, proving cleanup cost scales with retained unrelated entries

fix supplies caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest as --basetemp argument to nested pytest invocation, isolating session-finish cleanup without changing test selection, environment, timeout, or ambient-store assertions

regression test confirms nested pytest without private basetemp deletes another run's sentinel file in shared temp tree (RED), while fix preserves it (GREEN), and omitting basetemp again returns to RED
